correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge2\), all radii positive, the scalar H(t) is strictly increasing and has one root \(1\le t<(m+1)/2\). Unique reflection-invariant John ellipsoid follows from coordinate width maxima and explicit containment. The analytic equality \(\sum_i p_i=1/(tb^2)\), \(\sum_i a_i^2p_i=1\) proves entire-body containment and characterizes complete common-ridge tangency. Explicit two-orbit contact weights yield normalized mean zero and covariance \(I/(m+1)\), proving absolute Löwner optimality by the AM-GM determinant inequality, including uniqueness. The ratio monotonicity and sharp bounds follow from strict log-concavity and endpoint inequalities. From the actual standalone verifier: 330 cases residual at most 6.66e-16; 84 independent SLSQP solves maximum relative precision difference 8.66e-7. No finite test is substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The classical Steinmetz bicylinder and its high-dimensional rectangular-slice analogues form a canonical natural family with an outstanding exact approximation question. Complete John and Löwner semiaxes, continuous contact ridge, strict parameter monotonicity and sharp dimension-dependent volume spectrum give a structural and useful complete classification, rather than a generic exercise or isolated unmotivated number. The sharp bound is attained only as a genuine geometric degeneration.
